means: The classical framing rule that the subject sits about a third of the way across the frame rather than in the middle.
does: Nothing measurable on this model. The shot.comp.thirds_bias sweep rendered eight placement options at one fixed seed - center, left_third, right_third, golden_l, golden_r, symmetrical, edge_left, edge_right - and the subject is in effectively the same central position in ALL EIGHT panels. "rule of thirds" did not move him a third of the way anywhere, and "subject on the left third" did not either. This is the same failure family this project already measured with night and dark background: the tag describes a QUALITY of the arrangement instead of naming a THING, and SDXL has a strong centering prior plus no reliable left/right vocabulary to fight it with.
reach_for_it: don't. If the subject must be off-centre, do it deterministically - render wider than delivery and crop, or put a named object on the other side of the frame so the composition has a physical reason to shift.
used_in: the left_third and right_third options of shot.comp.thirds_bias, whose review already recommends cutting the card down and accepting that L/R cannot be fixed in the still pass
example_base: 1boy, solo, male focus, short dark hair, plain jacket, standing, city street, daytime
read_it_as: Compare the SHADING, colour and line - not the pose or framing. Adding any clause re-rolls the model's conditioning, so composition moves between the two panels even at a fixed seed. An img2img pass from one fixed base image would isolate the tag properly; that is not built yet.
